consensus_summary: Living water primarily signifies God’s life-giving gift, especially the Holy Spirit, bringing salvation and eternal life through Christ; the word or gospel is a recognized minority extension.
book_summary: Living water signifies both God’s Spirit and God’s word proceeding outward to impart life.
consensus_core_identification: The Holy Spirit as God’s life-giving saving gift.
book_core_identification: The outgoing Spirit and word of God as joint life-giving agencies.
boundary_disagreement: The book elevates the word of God from a minority or secondary interpretation to part of the term’s central identification alongside the Spirit. It also emphasizes their outward, life-giving action rather than primarily the gift received by believers.
material_contradiction: There is no direct contradiction because the book retains the consensus’s central identification with the Spirit. The difference is the material addition of God’s word as a co-referent.
rationale: The book preserves the dominant Spirit identification but broadens the core to include the word of God. Since word/gospel imagery already appears among recognized alternatives, the reading is not novel. The change is substantive enough to be REFINED rather than MATCH because it promotes a secondary interpretation into the defining core.
strongest_objection: John 7:38, especially when interpreted by John 7:39, supports the Spirit, while Jeremiah 2:13 identifies God as the fountain of living waters. Neither printed citation directly identifies living water with God’s word, so the book’s added co-referent is not established by these references alone.
